chunks: And it is narrated from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
that he said: 'Strike it (the animal) for fleeing, and do not strike it for stumbling.'

key_terms.النِّفَار: Nifar — the act of bolting or fleeing willfully; a deliberate escape from control
key_terms.الْعِثَار: Ithaar — stumbling, tripping; an involuntary physical mishap

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Islam to strike an animal for stumbling?
ai.summary: This brief prophetic tradition establishes an ethical distinction in the treatment of working animals: one may strike an animal that willfully bolts or flees, as that is a correctable behavioral defiance, but one must not strike an animal for stumbling, since stumbling is an involuntary mishap and not a fault of the animal. This teaching reflects the broader Islamic concern for animal welfare, distinguishing between disciplinary action and punishing an animal unjustly for something beyond its control.
